title: Arch v5 waves have no release dates
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 31-38; CONTEXT-20261116 project-context.md section 1
description: Arch v5 defines wave 0 (platform) and waves 1-4 by epic but gives no dates. The v2 context carries Release 1 30 November 2026, Release 2 31 December 2026 and Epic 3-8 monthly releases to June 2027 for the two-epic baseline. No source maps the five v5 waves to those releases.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 38 wave list; slide 31 overnight timeline; project-context.md v2 Release 1 and Release 2 rows; Template and Rules R1 U7 (dates unchanged and tentative)
proposed: Keep the dates unchanged and tentative, map waves 0-1 to Release 1 at the plan gate, and confirm the mapping in the verification loop

title: ADR-011 still describes one long case workflow
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 32 item 1 and slides 13-14; Architecture v5 slides 23-25; ADR-011
description: ADR-011 and Workflow Engine Design v3 describe one long CaseWorkflow with the route sets as states. The v5 design runs a parent CaseWorkflow with a child workflow per stage on the owning service's queue, Continue-As-New at every stage end and at least every 28 days, and parent close policy ABANDON.
evidence: Temporal and Drools design slide 13 parent-and-children diagram; slide 32 item 1 names ADR-011 as needing an update; Architecture v5 slides 23-25
proposed: Update ADR-011 to the parent-plus-stage-child model before Epic 3 starts

title: ADR-009 central log versus local record plus central ledger
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 28; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 32 item 2; ADR-009
description: ADR-009 writes the decision log synchronously inside every call and a failed write blocks the action. The v5 design writes the decision record, the state change and the outbox row in one local transaction, publishes DecisionRecorded, and seals the record in the central ledger in rwb-decision, with strict mode at points of no return. The change needs Risk and Internal Audit sign-off.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 28 notes (changes ADR-009); slide 20 every-service contract; Temporal and Drools design slide 14 step 7 and slide 32 item 2
proposed: Adopt RecordAndApply plus the central ledger and seal the change in ADR-022 after the Audit sign-off

title: Drools packages missing for S1 and S3-S9
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 5, 15 and 32 item 3; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4
description: Only RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH and BOOKING_MATCH exist as Phase 1 Drools packages. The 448 rules exist in ten route sets (RES 37, SET 27, DIL 37, GUA 32, LIT 79, DIS 72, DS 41, WO 51, DEV 22, UNI 50) but the package codes for S1 and S3-S9 are Phase 2 and no owning service is nominated in the rule source.
evidence: Temporal and Drools design slide 5 notes (Phase 1 and Phase 2 packages); slide 15 Phase 1 package list; slide 32 item 3
proposed: One package per route set, owned by the service named in the Ownership Map, delivered in the epic that starts that service

title: Route numbering R4 and R5 conflict
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 17 and 20 notes; Case Journeys v3; Routing Logic v4
description: R-LIT-01 starts litigation on route R4, while Case Journeys v3 calls R4 the guarantee claim and R5 litigation. Both sources are below the Arch v5 catalogue in R-PREC, so the conflict survives.
evidence: Temporal and Drools design slide 20 notes; slide 17 open point; Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-01
proposed: Keep the rule text as written and name the route per Case Journeys v3 until the route map is re-issued

title: Rule format XLS decision tables or DMN 1.6
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 27; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 15 and 32 item 5; ADR-012
description: ADR-012 and the Phase 1 build use Drools XLS decision tables stored in the database. The v5 deck proposes OMG DMN 1.6 decision models, converted table by table on the same Drools runtime. The choice is not decided.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 27 notes; Temporal and Drools design slide 15 notes and slide 32 item 5
proposed: Keep XLS tables for the Phase 1 packages and convert one table at a time, with both formats on the same runtime

title: Temporal version 1.30+, 1.28.1 and 1.29.7
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 23; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 32 item 6; ADR-011; local stack
description: v5 requires Temporal 1.30 or later for Nexus and Worker Versioning; ADR-011 pins 1.28.1; the local demonstration stack runs 1.29.7. The upgrade owner and date are not set.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 23 notes (upgrade from 1.28.1 to 1.30); slide 47 risk row; Temporal and Drools design slide 31 notes (1.29.7) and slide 32 item 6
proposed: Upgrade to 1.30 or later in wave 0 before any worker is built

title: JOB-16 write-off scan trigger
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 23 notes; Batch and Scheduling Design v4
description: JOB-16 is a Temporal Schedule on the 3rd working day in rwb-writeoff in one source, starts on the ACE batch-complete record in Batch and Scheduling Design v4, and is kept on Quartz by the T2 note. The Ownership Map records S7 with a Temporal Schedule.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 job map; Temporal and Drools design slide 23 notes; Ownership Map ruling ASM-A6-flows-12
proposed: Temporal Schedule in rwb-writeoff, monthly on the 3rd working day, triggered after AceDataReady

title: Airflow role and ownership undecided
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 5, 8, 31, 32 and 39
description: The bank Airflow is marked for discussion: who owns the DAGs, when Control-M moves to Airflow, where Airflow runs, and which ADR replaces the BRD's ADF and Control-M wording are all open. The recommended use is the cross-system chain, file windows, report extracts and one-off bulk work, with service APIs only.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 32 notes (to agree); slide 39 decision 1-6 list; slide 8 platform row; slide 47 risk list
owner_role: Enterprise Architecture and bank platform team
proposed: Record Airflow at Recovery's edges only and keep the Control-M poll as the fallback until a new ADR replaces the BRD wording

title: BOT approval route under FPG 19/2560 clause 5.5
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 6, 38, 39 decision 6, 50
description: Whether the move to 19 services is a significant change that needs a board-approved plan and prior BOT approval is undecided; the lead time is up to 30 business days and Compliance confirms the route. The submission date is a programme dependency.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 6 notes (clause 5.5); slide 39 decision 6; slide 50 programme dependency
proposed: Confirm the route in wave 0 and place the submission date in the programme plan

title: Kafka hosting not confirmed
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 21, 39 decision 1 and 47
description: Kafka on the bank platform is the recommendation, with Azure Event Hubs Premium as the fallback. Capacity, topic naming, the ACL model, the schema registry and the environments are still to agree with the ACE platform team.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 21 notes (to confirm); slide 39 decision 1; slide 47 risk row 'Kafka platform not ready'
owner_role: Enterprise Architecture and ACE platform team
proposed: Reserve the dedicated topics and ACLs in wave 0 and keep the outbox and the Event Hubs fallback

title: 19 schemas, logins and the connection budget are not created
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 29 and 39 decision 2
description: The design needs 19 schemas and 19 logins on the ACE PostgreSQL server, each with a PgBouncer pool and a connection cap. Neither the creation nor the per-login connection budget is recorded in a source.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 29 (PgBouncer pool and connection cap per login); slide 39 decision 2; slide 47 risk row 'ACE database capacity'
proposed: Create the schemas and logins in wave 0 and set the cap per login with the ACE DBA

title: ACE Common contracts are not versioned or scheduled
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 30 and 39 decision 4
description: Six ACE Common connections (sign-in, audit and PII logging, shared case view, restructure calculator, notification path, shared entities) are consumed through contracts under INT-34, but no version, schedule or contract-test arrangement is recorded.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 30 notes; slide 39 decision 4; slide 47 risk row 'ACE Common contracts change'
proposed: Version each of the six contracts and run contract tests on both sides from wave 1

title: Table inventory does not cover the v5 schema-per-service model and the FK cuts are empty
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables and sheet FK cuts; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17-20 and 41
description: The 93 tables come from Physical Schema v6. S1 has no table in the map although slide 18 gives rwb_valuation three object groups (valuations, the D6 route decision, route-agent output); P8 has one table (proceeds) although slide 17 gives payment and proceeds matching, fees, bookings and posting files; the FK-cut sheet has no rows even though no cross-schema key is allowed.
evidence: Ownership Map sheet Tables (93 rows) and sheet FK cuts (header only); Architecture v5 slide 17 P8 DB line; slide 18 S1 DB line; slide 29 no cross-schema rule
proposed: Add the v5 tables for S1 and P8 and populate the FK cuts as ID references in the next Ownership Map version

title: RPO and RTO are not set
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 48; NFR Spec v3; CONTEXT-20261116 project-context.md section 7
description: Slide 48 records 'RPO/RTO: not yet set' as an NFR gap. The v2 context assumed 15 minutes RPO and 4 hours RTO. No approved target exists.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 48 service targets and notes; project-context.md v2 RPO/RTO row
proposed: Leave RPO/RTO unset in the baseline and confirm the tiers with Compliance before the release gate

title: Volumes differ between the v2 context and v5
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 33 and 48; CONTEXT-20261116 project-context.md sections 1 and 7
description: The v2 context says about 45,000 recovery cases a year, about 180 recovery users and 1,500 documents a day. v5 gives 23,570 open cases today and 47,389 by 2031, about 3,110 new cases a month, 414 concurrent staff, 320 partner users with 48 concurrent, and 64-74k documents a month.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 33 and slide 48 notes (Volume and Scale Forecast v3, NFR Spec v3); project-context.md v2 Case volume and Staff rows
proposed: Use the v5 Volume and Scale Forecast v3 figures and retire the v2 rows

title: No v5 screen inventory or screen-to-service map
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10 and 20; CONTEXT-20261116 frontend-context.md
description: Arch v5 states the edge behaviour (one hop from gateway-bff, 2 s timeout, tabs load on click, about 1.2 s budget) but gives no screen inventory, no screen-to-service map and no design system. The 53 screens and the design tokens in frontend-context.md v2 are not restated in v5.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 10 walkthrough; slide 20 gateway-bff contract; frontend-context.md v2; no v5 screen source in the read set
proposed: Derive the screen-to-service map from the gateway-bff composite routes and record it in frontend-context.md in the next context run

title: Platform task queue rwb-platform is not one of the 19 services
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 sheet Jobs (JOB-21, JOB-22); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20, 41 and 44
description: JOB-21 (stuck workflow scan) and JOB-22 (platform smoke) are recorded on a platform task queue named rwb-platform, with PlatformSmokeWorkflow. Arch v5 names task queues only for the 19 services and slices 41 and 44 name the owner as 'platform' or 'all'.
evidence: Ownership Map jobs JOB-21 and JOB-22 replacement text; Architecture v5 slide 44; slide 41 task-queue column
proposed: Record rwb-platform as a shared platform queue in namespace rwb-recovery and confirm it with the platform team

title: The canonical context files remain at v2
source: CONTEXT-20261116 context package (project-context.md, backend-context.md, frontend-context.md, testing-standards.md, domain-context.md); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
description: The five canonical context files describe one service, schema recovery, 93 tables in that schema, Quartz and Spring Batch jobs, about 45,000 cases a year and an assumed RPO of 15 minutes. D-RCV-60 replaces those statements with 19 services, a schema and login per service, Kafka events, Temporal Schedules and the v5 volumes.
evidence: project-context.md v2 sections 4, 5, 7, 11 and 19; backend-context.md v2 sections 1-4; testing-standards.md v2; Architecture v5 slides 1, 29 and 38
proposed: Re-base project-context.md, backend-context.md, frontend-context.md and testing-standards.md on this file in the next context run

title: Regulatory source dates and coverage
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 6, 50 and 51
description: The AI Risk Management Guidelines date (12 September 2025) comes from a secondary source; it is not checked whether later rules supersede FPG 19/2559; CRAF has no standalone document on the BOT site and is taken from a payment-systems report. Compliance owns the interpretation.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 6 notes; slide 50 notes; slide 51 verification notes
proposed: Compliance confirms the three citations before the wave 1 gate

title: Testing standards lack the v5 test obligations
source: CONTEXT-20261116 testing-standards.md; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 22, 29 and 46; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 27
description: The v5 design requires contract tests per API, event and activity, Temporal replay tests and the replay gate E2-040, Testcontainers for Kafka and PostgreSQL, the daily journey smoke workflow JOB-22, at least 50 scenarios per rule package and a boundary test on every build. testing-standards.md v2 has Testcontainers PostgreSQL but no Kafka, no replay gate and no JOB-22.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11 (contract tests in every build); slide 29 (boundary test); slide 46 (test approach); Temporal and Drools design slide 15 (50 scenarios) and slide 27 (replay gate)
proposed: Add the five test obligations to testing-standards.md in the next context run

title: TimerDue owner recorded as P3 and as PLT
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 sheet Events and sheet Rulings; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42
description: EV-18 TimerDue is recorded as retired with the producer 'durable timer'. The events sheet and the flow ruling name PLT as owner, while an earlier API ruling names P3 as the service that hosts case timers and publishes TimerBreached.
evidence: Ownership Map events row EV-18; rulings ASM-A6-flows-2 and ASM-A6-api-7; Architecture v5 slide 42 row 18
proposed: Keep PLT as the owner of the retired event and leave TimerBreached (EV-19) with P3
